fairnessNotes: Even-handed. Rosenblatt is credited as the psychologist whose project the Mark I was ('the project of psychologist Frank Rosenblatt'), not as its sole builder. He is shown as an anonymous era silhouette in shirtsleeves, upright and attentive, with an accurate role card and no likeness or quotation (the brief forbids quotes; quotes.json is empty and none are used). Minsky and Papert appear only as a dated stamp with no likeness. They are credited with a correct result ('showed just how simple') and not cast as villains. The contested 'Perceptrons killed neural networks' story is avoided. The line sets two true facts side by side (the book showed the limit; interest faded for years) with no causal verb. That leaves some room for a post-hoc reading, but it is within limit-linear's 'often thought to have contributed' and is acceptable for a one-minute short. No lab, company or nation is named or favoured in the lineage line. The title's 'learned to see' is a period-flavoured overstatement, and the film balances it explicitly with 'It could learn only simple patterns'. The simplified board (about 64 dials, direct cell-to-dial threads) is labelled 'an illustration of the rule', so the teaching model is not passed off as the hardware.
best_moments: ch01-s03 at 42-47 s: the real seeded run plays out with every readout agreeing. Try 3 is wrong, try 4 (vertical) is right, and try 5 (horizontal) is right with the 'now / then' ghost of try 1. The film shows learning on two different shapes, not one lucky guess, which is exactly what mk1-rule and mk1-trained support.

ch01-s03 at 51.0 s: on 'It could learn only simple patterns' the machine goes quiet, and the two learned shapes stand apart under 'what it could learn: simple patterns'. The film states the limit honestly without inventing a failure case it never ran.

ch01-s03 at 26.5-36.9 s: the 'correct answer: horizontal' tag beside the retina, the 'threshold' tick on the gauge and 'try 1 · said vertical · WRONG' over the nudged dials make 'Nobody gave it the rule' true on screen. The machine is shown being told the answer after it guesses, and it is never shown being given the rule.
